note: Files the template distributes to repos that `biffo core upgrade` cannot reach. Instances carry biffo.core.json and a core-manifest.json, so they are upgraded by the CLI's three-way merge. Sibling apps (biffo.sibling.json) and plugin repos (biffo.plugin.json) are SEPARATE REPOSITORIES with neither, and until 2026-07-29 the only documented channel to them was 'vendor into the skeleton, plus a one-time manual copy-in for existing ones'. That is not a mechanism, it is a hope: the skeleton only helps repos created afterwards, and nothing ever prompts the copy-in. It is how AGENTS.md drifted 68 lines behind in tabsii (#559), and how eight repos ended up running a local gate two versions old that checked one thing in eight (#855). scripts/shared-sync.sh reads this list, reports drift with --check, and opens a PR per repo without it. Add a file here only if every sibling and plugin should have the template's copy verbatim -- this is a one-way overwrite, not a merge, so nothing a repo is expected to customise belongs in it. Scope is any repo carrying one of `appliesTo`'s markers OR any repo that already holds scripts/verify.sh: the runner repos have neither marker but did receive the gate, and distributing a file once then losing track of it recreates the drift this exists to end. scripts/shared-sync.sh additionally writes .biffo-shared-version into each target -- the template core version the files came from, read from the TEMPLATE and never from the target, so it cannot report perfect health by comparing a repo to itself. The two dependency-audit scripts were added for #743: this repo hardened its own audits in #591/#592/#636/#717/#721 and both skeletons kept shipping the raw `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` / `uv run pip-audit`, so every satellite was born reddening a required check on any registry hiccup. They qualify as verbatim content because they take their target from the CI job's working directory rather than from a repo layout -- one byte-identical file is correct in this repo's root, in a sibling's apps/frontend and services/api, and in a plugin repo's root alike. js-dependency-audit.sh lands in Python-only plugin repos too and is simply never invoked there; that is the price of a one-way overwrite with no per-repo conditionals, and it is cheaper than the conditionals.
filesIfPresentNote: Files kept in step ONLY in repos that already hold them -- never created. Mapping is `target path in the satellite` -> `canonical copy in this repo`, because unlike `files` the two are not the same path: a sibling's apps/frontend/... has no counterpart at this repo's root (there is apps/portal/ and no apps/frontend/), so the skeleton IS the canonical copy. Added for #1107: `handleResponse` threw the entire response body as the error message, so a user saw `{"detail":"Administrator access required"}` where a page's content belonged. The identical function was in the skeleton and in all seven siblings, and `files` could not carry it: it CREATES what is absent, so it would have written a frontend API client into two plugin repos, two runner repos and a design repo that have no frontend at all -- and shared-files-parity.test.ts requires every `files` entry in EVERY skeleton, which apps/frontend/... can never satisfy in plugin-template. The mechanism can still backfill, deliberately: that is what `files` is for. This list is how you say a file must not be created, only kept current -- because putting a file into a repo that never had one is a decision somebody should make, not a side effect of adding a line to a manifest. Reconciling a file first is part of the price of entry: apps/frontend/src/lib/auth.ts is present in all seven siblings and diverges by 29-247 lines, so a one-way overwrite would clobber whichever behaviour is correct -- see #1117 before adding it.
supersedesNote: Raw commands each shared script replaces, checked by scripts/ci-wiring-audit.sh. shared-sync.sh gets the script INTO a repo; nothing made the repo call it, and on 2026-07-29 eleven repos merged the scripts and every one carried on running the raw command -- drift went to zero and the outcome did not move (#884). ci.yml cannot be a one-way overwrite because the path depends on that step's working-directory, so the mechanism is an assertion rather than a copy: you cannot write the line for the repo, but you can refuse to let it forget. Add a pair here whenever a shared script supersedes a command repos invoke directly; the check only fires in repos that actually hold the script, so a repo shared-sync has not reached yet is reported once, by shared-sync, rather than twice.
